rule.description: A class method whose data access is dominated by one foreign object - a parameter, an alias of a parameter, or fields destructured out of one - while barely touching its own instance state. The method holds misplaced behavior and belongs on the object whose data it consumes.

checks.description: Detect class methods that repeatedly reach into one foreign data owner while barely touching their own instance state.
checks.detected_relation: host method -> per-message entry record / language pack / i18n instance foreign data
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The behavior is dominated by another object's data (hits, cache writes, market conventions, journal metrics, instance fields), so the responsibility is mislocated; moving it to the data owner restores data locality.

matches.evidence: Diagnostic description line is assembled entirely from the per-message entry record, touching no I18N state.
The pack report exposes the language pack's own counters, market conventions and hot window without consulting the I18N instance.
The promotion decision reads only the entry's hotness, hit, cache-write and usage timestamps; the pack contributes none of its own state.
Rendering pulls the entry's content, language, last-rendered language and key, and mutates render bookkeeping on the entry.
Currency, grouping, fraction digits and the target locale are all market facts of the language pack; the formatter adds only default merging.
The cache key, hot-slot marking and the cache-write counter all derive from the entry record.
Prunability is decided from the entry's hit count, hotness, identity and usage stamps; the cache only supplements its slot ownership.
The usage journal line inlines the entry's key, language, hits, hotness, cache writes, last use and render sequence.
The instance snapshot reads the language, packs, active keys, default key, entry registry and cache counters straight off the i18n instance.

excluded.reason: Path helper from the original codebase: 5 reads spread over two different parameter owners and both stay below the single-owner threshold.
Options-merging helper reads each caller-supplied field once (5 reads on one parameter); constructing a working options record is not reaching into a neighboring object.
Integration hub: it creates and touches the entry/pack collaborators through this-wired calls rather than reading one foreign owner's fields in bulk.
